chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: American television appearances and rifts with Burns and Allen
summary: He lists early US TV shows such as the Kate Smith Hour and Perry Como and says only Burns and Allen had billing and dressing-room rifts.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Did you see yourself eventually on television?
No.
Did you want to see yourself on television?
That was the first broadcast there, but I'd been on television in America. That was the first television broadcast from England that they ever had. But America, I'd been on television in America.
What television had you been on?

I'd been on the Kate Smith Hour, I'd been on the Ford Hour, I'd been on the Windows of the World, I'd been on the -- this girl named Emerson had a program -- Faye Emerson I think it was. She had a television program. I was on that one. I was on the
-- what's his name? Perry Como. I'd been on all the television shows in America.
Was this Buck and Bubbles or just you?
Yeah, Buck and Bubbles.
And you did your routine there, too?
No, I just did a couple of numbers.
So this was back -- what time that you were doing these television shows? This is prior to "Porgy and Bess?"
I did some prior to "Porgy and Bess," did some after, too.
So you were also meeting a lot of new television personalities --
Oh, yeah, I met all you could think of.
Were these
Variety shows.
Mh-hm, I met quite a few people in the business.
Can you tell me about anything that stands out in your mind about any people that you met? Is there perhaps some experience that you had with them that you can recall?

Burns and Allen are about the only ones I know that I met concerning anything, any rifts concerning the theater about billing and dressing rooms and all that stuff. That's the only two people. We got over that, we got over that one, we got over all of 'em. They were all simple.
